title: Courses and teachers at Greenwald
summary: Nine-to-three days of history and music theory, arranging, piano and voice, with teachers Mr. Dean and Ms. Moulton.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So was this like a regular school, you went nine to five?
Right. Nine, well, I went from nine to three, every day.
And what courses did you take? What did you have?

Well, we had American history, we had medieval history, we had music, and I think it was four courses we took. What was the other one? You know, I can't think about it. I'm going to make sure that I tell you, because this was very interesting. Like I said, we were taught on a college level. And I had some notes somewhere around here, because I didn't throw that away. I figured this would eventually come back, what I had to talk about, and I kept it. But the things that we were taught that they didn't teach today. You know, just prepare you to be a musician. And you know, so they were teaching, they taught other courses. Besides music. Besides music, yeah.
That you had to take to graduate. Right, right. But specifically, do you remember which music courses? Was it like the theory?

Oh yeah, it was theory. We had theory, then we had advanced theory, we had, oh, what is music into mathematics? That's the one I wasn't good at because I never was good at mathematics. What did you call it? Oh.

No, not counterpoint, no. Oh, man. But anyway, we took this, I never was good at this particular subject, because it was music into mathematics. I can't think of that. But like I said, it was theory, advanced theory, arranging, and then I had my piano, you know. And then I had voice lessons.
Who taught you, did you have a different teacher for each subject? Yeah. Did you remember who the teachers were there?

Mr. Dean was one of the arranging teachers. Ms. Moulton. Ms. Moulton was a voice teacher. What was this little lady? Or the lady that taught piano to me was Ms. Moulton. Ms. Moulton. She's from Xavier University. She taught me. I got private piano. So you know what was that? The lady that taught piano to me was from Ms. Moulton. Ms. Moulton. She's from Xavier University. She taught me. I got private piano lessons every day, one album every day. Who was our arrangement? We had a theory teacher, we had an advanced theory teacher. See, there was theory and then it was advanced theory. Because after you got a theory class and you took the advanced theory, and then there was arranging and then there was advanced arranging. So you see like I said, a background that I had musically is really responsible for me being able to be a band leader today. Because a lot of things, see a lot of things I had to put to work here.
